column1: # The Gospel of each day in the Roman Rite, after the Ordo Lectionum Missae,
# editio typica altera (1981), with the later additions to the General Roman
# Calendar. build_lectionary.py checks every reference against the verse
# One line per day: a key, then its Gospels, separated by tabs. The keys are
# the ones src/liturgy.js gives a day; "@A", "@B" or "@C" ties a line to that
# Sunday cycle, and a line without one serves every year. Each Gospel may
# carry labels before a colon ("vigil:", "passion,short:"), named in
# src/i18n.js under `liturgy.labels`; a "*" marks the one shown first when it
# is not the first. Verse letters (5a, 12b) keep the reference as the
# Lectionary prints it; the reader shows those verses whole.
# Verse numbers are those of the Nova Vulgata, which are the rows of the
# Advent: weekdays to December 16, then by date
# Lent: Sundays. In Years B and C the Gospels of Year A may be read on the
# Lent: weekdays. In the Third, Fourth and Fifth Weeks, the Mass of that
# week's Year A Gospel may be said on any weekday.
# Solemnities and memorials of the Lord and of Mary after Pentecost
# Ordinary Time: Sundays (the First is the Baptism of the Lord, the
# Ordinary Time: weekdays, the same in Years I and II. Mark is read in
# Weeks 1 to 9, Matthew in 10 to 21, Luke in 22 to 34.
# Saints: the solemnities, the feasts, and the obligatory memorials that
# have a Gospel of their own (other memorials keep the weekday's Gospel).
